title: OAuthFlow
description: Subscription-connect flow state. RUNTIME-DECLARED presentation (S1 gap ③): the server declares what to show and what it expects back; the UI renders declaratively and never keys off a vendor→form table. UI shell semantics mirror the existing BackendOAuthPanel (2s poll, 15-min timeout, cancel). Forms A/B/C from spec §5 frame 09 are presentation patterns the declaration composes: A = auth_url + expects paste_code; B = auth_url + device_code + expects none; C = auth_url + expects paste_callback_url. Under Option 1, native_cli subscription connect drives the CLI's own login through this same shape.

intent.description: v2 (07-29, review round 6): what this flow is FOR, and therefore what its terminal success response carries — `create` → `{flow, source, adopted_by}`, `reauth` → `{flow, source, recovered, interrupted_pairs}` (api.md → OAuth completion responses). Round 5 defined neither, which left the two creation paths inconsistent: `POST /sources` closed the 「so what now?」 loop with `adopted_by` while the OAuth door — the default way a subscription is added — returned only flow state. Declared as a field rather than inferred, for two reasons. `source_id` cannot discriminate: hub-channel CREATE flows also set it, for the pending source they bind to, so both intents can carry one. And the alternative — the client remembering which button it pressed — makes the response shape a function of client state instead of of the payload, which is exactly how a poll that arrives after a page reload ends up parsed as the wrong shape. OPTIONAL here, REQUIRED at the API boundary from v2 on (README → required-vs-optional): the shipped flow payloads are validated against this file by tests/test_model_hub_api.py and predate the field, so a `required` would fail the contract gate instead of tightening it.

source_id.description: v1.1: pending Source this flow binds to (deterministic association; hub-channel flows always set it)

channel.description: where the resulting credential will live; hub-held subscriptions only behind the consent-gated experimental flag (S2)
